=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:282-317, 390-405 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Train-internal label removals, and a failed queue-label POST, can leave the `<!-- merge-train:queued -->` marker in place so the next gate evaluation treats the state as a human-initiated bypass.
  WHY: A stale marker with no `ai:merge-queued` label can let a PR proceed despite newly reappearing blockers, reintroducing the concurrent same-file collision the train is intended to prevent.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:16623-16636; scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1545, 1582-1586 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: Stall recovery does not recognize `ai:merge-queued` PRs that are intentionally waiting in the `ai:done` phase.
  WHY: After `STALL_THRESHOLD_DONE_MINUTES=120`, the poller can push repeated empty commits, trigger false stall alerts and judge calls, and burn review-runner minutes on queued PRs.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:396-400 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: `_mt_upsert_comment` is called unguarded after a successful claim and dispatch, so a transient marker-lookup failure aborts the release loop under `set -e`.
  WHY: A cosmetic comment failure converts a successful release into a partial release, leaving remaining queued PRs unexamined until a later poll tick or close event.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:41-48, 290 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: The API-budget header omits the paginated comments-list REST call performed by `_mt_find_marker_comment_id` on every gate evaluation with non-empty blockers.
  WHY: The documented rate-limit cost undercounts the actual API usage by one REST call per queued gate evaluation.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3181; .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:169-170 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: Workflow comments state that `cancel_on_pr_close.yml` releases the queue “on merge” or “on a merged” PR even though the removed condition makes release run on every PR close.
  WHY: The stale comments mislead operators about the effective trigger contract when diagnosing releases after unmerged PR closes.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The poller should skip ai:merge-queued PRs to avoid dispatching resolver rounds the train is holding back
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:16630 adds logic to skip merge-train queued PRs in the in-progress conflict-dispatch loop, but no test in tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py verifies this behavior; the grep for "ai:merge-queued" in test_orchestrate_poll*.py returned no results.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:396-400 (_mt_release, the success branch calling _mt_upsert_comment) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After a successful claim+dispatch, `_mt_upsert_comment` is called with 3 positional arguments (no pre-fetched comment id). When its internal `_mt_find_marker_comment_id` call fails transiently (line 228), `_mt_upsert_comment` returns 1.
  WHY: Under the toplevel `set -e` (line 60), this non-zero return aborts `_mt_release`'s while-loop, leaving remaining queued PRs unexamined until the next poll tick or close event.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3181 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The step comment says "cancel_on_pr_close.yml (on merge) and orchestrate_poll.yml (every tick) release the queue," but the LAST RUN DIFF removed the `if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true` condition so release now runs on every PR close, not only on merge.
  WHY: No runtime failure; the comment misstates the trigger contract and can mislead operators debugging releases for unmerged closes.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:169-170 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The backstop step comment says "The event path (cancel_on_pr_close.yml on a merged ai/issue-* PR) releases queued PRs immediately," but the code now fires on every PR close.
  WHY: No runtime defect; stale documentation only.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:41-48 (API budget header comment) vs. 290 (_mt_gate calling _mt_find_marker_comment_id) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The header says gate costs "+1-2 comment calls only when the queued state or blocker set changes," but `_mt_find_marker_comment_id` at line 290 performs a paginated comments-list REST call on every gate evaluation with non-empty blockers.
  WHY: The documented rate-limit budget undercounts by one REST call per queued gate evaluation.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:_mt_gate lines 307-317, unblocked branch lines 284-287, release path lines 392-405, bypass branch lines 294-300 | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The one-shot bypass is keyed on "label absent + <!-- merge-train:queued --> marker present", but the train itself creates that state without any human action.
  WHY: A transient GitHub API failure or train-internal label removal can silently disable the merge train and let the review proceed against older overlapping PRs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:16623-16636; scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1582-1586, threshold 1545 ("ai:done": 120), and the retrigger_review path whose own comment at orchestrate_poll_process.sh:13141-13148 | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A merge-queued PR's issue deliberately stays in the ai:done phase with no active review run and no fresh pushes, but the ai:done stall ladder has no merge-queued awareness.
  WHY: Every queued PR that waits behind an older overlapping PR longer than two hours can accumulate empty "re-trigger" commits, repeated false stall alerts, wasted review dispatches and judge calls, up to MAX_STALL_RECOVERIES_DONE=99 times.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:_mt_upsert_comment lines 224-230 called unguarded from _mt_release line 397 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The last run changed _mt_upsert_comment to return 1 when the marker-lookup API call fails, and the release success path at line 397 calls it inside a block subject to `set -euo pipefail`.
  WHY: A transient comments-list failure after a successful claim + dispatch aborts the whole script before evaluating the remaining queued PRs.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:42-47 vs. the _mt_find_marker_comment_id call at line 290 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The documented gate budget ("1 list call + files calls ... +1 label call and +1-2 comment calls only when the queued state or blocker set changes") omits the comments-list REST call performed on every gate evaluation with non-empty blockers.
  WHY: Operators sizing API budgets from the header get a wrong figure.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml and .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml: review_autofix.yml "Merge-train gate" step comment and orchestrate_poll.yml "Release merge-queued PRs (merge train backstop)" step comment | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Both workflow comments declare the event path as firing only on a merged PR, but the last run removed the `if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true` condition so release now fires on every PR close.
  WHY: An operator reading the YAML is misled about the actual trigger contract.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:282-288 (unblocked path) and scripts/review_merge_train.sh:390-405 (release path); bypass logic at lines 294-301 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the train removes the `ai:merge-queued` label, the `<!-- merge-train:queued -->` marker comment is not removed or updated.
  WHY: If blockers reappear after the train released the PR, the next gate run sees no label plus a stale queued marker and incorrectly treats this state as a bypass, allowing the PR to proceed unqueued against the new blocker.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py: no matching test for scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:16630 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR diff adds logic to skip merge-train queued PRs in the in-progress conflict-dispatch loop, but no test verifies this behavior.
  WHY: The grep for "ai:merge-queued" in test_orchestrate_poll*.py returned no results.
